svg.title: VeriCommons full stack: two layers, provers, zkTLS, zkPass adapter, delayed attribution, ERC-4337
svg.desc: Merged architecture. Layer 2 is the plaza wrapper. Layer 1 is the reusable kernel (prove, verify, issue). Provers include self-hosted Public Web, official APIs, zkTLS vendors, and onchain. zkPass is a vendor product adapted with a recorded trust assumption. Delayed attribution is a kernel fact, not zkTLS. ERC-4337 can consume tickets and can be an onchain source.
svg.text: Two layers on top. Backend-neutral provers underneath (self-host + vendor adapters). zkTLS is a technique, not our product. Delayed attribution is not zkTLS. 4337 consumes tickets and can be proven on-chain.
LAYER 2 packages/task plaza wrapper not required to reuse the kernel
Binds a kernel ticket to a plaza task. Owns taskId, caps, PENDING, credit hook. Does not talk to zkPass.
LAYER 1 packages/kernel independent directory same 3 steps as a zkPass-style kernel
Core value: one entry ticket, swap provers, record trust. Others can import this package without the plaza wrapper.
fact: B qualified via channel A
kernel owns the fact; task layer uses it
PROVERS = backend-neutral backend = this row. kernel.prove() dispatches here.
Compatible: any engine whose verify-result we can map. Self-hosted provers do not need a vendor to cooperate. Vendor adapters trust their SDK and record verifierSet.
we call their API, we sign
zkTLS = a TECHNIQUE inside the prover row, not a VeriCommons product layer
Several vendors implement it. We do not have to own a zkTLS stack. We can self-host TLSNotary later.
we ADAPT, we do not control
SOURCES - facts in the world. No HTTPS endpoint = cannot use zkTLS; use delayed attribution.
no observable HTTPS - delayed path only
Immediate: GitHub / Public Web / zkTLS vendor - prove now - verify now - issue - PASS
Delayed: no prover can fetch Moments - skip zk - PENDING + channel id - later result - issue - PASS
We cannot re-run their TLS. After their SDK says OK, we issue OUR ticket
with verifierSet = zkPass (or Reclaim). Explicit trust assumption, recorded.
Could we build a zkPass-like login product on the kernel? Yes, by adding our zkTLS + UX. Not required for the plaza.
Same 3 steps, bundled with their engine + app. We plug in at verify-result, not inside their TLS.
Adapter maps that verify-result into kernel.issue().
Possible. Offline Evidence can replace some login / policy checks.
3. Validator / paymaster / session key checks it
Chain must NOT verify a full zkTLS blob in UserOp.
It checks issuer signature or a stored ticket hash.
Replaces some policy. Does not replace UserOp signature.
Standard vs custom 4337: same kernel, different module.
Web2 fact stays off-chain. 4337 only sees the entry ticket.
Arrow B - 4337 is a SOURCE of facts
Possible. Web3 credentials are the easy proofs.
Onchain prover reads owner, module, UserOp, token/NFT, logs.
A relayer reads chain state; kernel.issue() the ticket.
Account may EIP-1271-sign subject binding (control, not GitHub).
HTTPS, GitHub, WeChat, zkPass TLS session.
Contracts cannot fetch Web2. Bind Web2 tickets via Arrow A.
The account does not generate zkTLS. It is a subject and a signer.
Custom 4337 vs standard: same. Difference is validator modules.
